events.title: T-Mobile Sidekick released
events.summary: T-Mobile began selling the Danger Hiptop (Sidekick) in October 2002 — a swivel-screen smartphone aimed at messaging and mobile web.
events.about: The Sidekick's cloud-backed address book, AIM chat, and mobile browser made it a cult device for early mobile social networking. Its app ecosystem and always-on data plan influenced how carriers thought about smartphone subsidies. Developers built [Java] ME apps and mobile web experiences for a youth audience years before the App Store.

narrative.whyChosen: The Sidekick popularized always-on mobile messaging and cloud-synced contacts for consumers.
narrative.whyImportant: It showed non-enterprise users would pay for data plans to stay connected on a pocket device.
narrative.problemSolved: Feature phones offered poor mobile web and no integrated instant messaging experience.
